slides.texte_overlay:
How to become extremely good
at first dates in your 20s
Choose the place with care. Somewhere a bit quiet where you can actually hear each other. A loud club makes every first date much harder than it needs to be.
Be on time, and text if you're running late. Respecting her time is the first thing she'll notice. Arriving relaxed and early sets the tone for the whole evening.
Ask about her world, then really listen. Her job, her city, her favourite weekend. Follow-up questions show real interest far more than any rehearsed line.
Share something real about yourself. A passion, a funny failure, a dream. Opening up a little makes the date feel like a real conversation, not an interview.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. You'll never run out of interesting things to talk about on a first date again, wherever you go.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. You'll never run out of interesting things to say again.

slides.texte_overlay: Keep your phone in your pocket the entire time. Full attention is rare and attractive. Checking your phone just once can undo an hour of great conversation.
End clearly. If you had fun, say so: "I'd love to see you again." If not, thank her warmly. Honesty at the end of a first date is a clear sign of real maturity.
